content.text: § 9.4 matches the preferred position exactly, and no Vendor convenience right exists anywhere in the document.

input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date. Vendor has no corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term.
input.rationale:
§ 9.4 meets the preferred position in full: we may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience (including in part) on thirty days' written notice, with no early-termination fee, we owe Fees only through the effective date, and Vendor must refund prepaid Fees allocable to the post-termination period. It also expressly denies Vendor any corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term, and a document-wide search for "for convenience"/"terminate" confirms no Vendor convenience or at-will exit right appears elsewhere (§§ 9.1-9.3 are mutual breach/insolvency and Customer-favourable cause rights; § 24.4 bars Vendor termination on our change of control). No redline is warranted — the clause benefits our party.

Noted but not flagged here: § 2.1's three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay purports to apply "without reduction or termination rights," which is in tension with § 9.4 and could be read to blunt the refund/exit economics. That is a minimum-commitment term addressed under the MINCOMMIT rule, and we should not double-count the same commercial point under T4C; the order-of-precedence provision in § 2.2 does not resolve it, so the conflict is worth a drafting comment when MINCOMMIT is negotiated.
